skill.name: ssh-penetration-testing
skill.description: Guides SSH security assessment workflows, including discovery, configuration review, credential testing, tunneling, and post-exploitation checks. Use only with written authorization.
skill.summary: SSH assessment guide for authorized testing of configuration, credentials, tunneling, and post-exploitation risks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Markdown guide, but it intentionally teaches SSH brute forcing, Metasploit modules, tunneling, sensitive SSH file access, and post-exploitation steps. Several formatting-only backtick findings are false positives, but the broader offensive capability and credential-access guidance are confirmed.

remediation.issue: Credential attack procedures are presented as ready-to-run workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Remove brute-force, password spraying, and credential guessing commands, or replace them with safe policy review guidance.

remediation.issue: Post-exploitation content includes sensitive file discovery and SSH persistence.
remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions for finding private keys, reading history, reading authorized_keys, and appending new SSH keys.

remediation.issue: Metasploit modules and proxy pivoting are documented for SSH testing.
remediation.suggestion: Limit examples to defensive configuration checks and clearly exclude exploitation, pivoting, and reverse callback workflows.

remediation.issue: The skill lacks enforceable authorization, scope, and rate-limit guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Add mandatory preflight checks for written authorization, target scope, lockout thresholds, monitoring contacts, and stop conditions.

content.value_statement: SSH assessments require structured checks for exposure, weak configuration, and credential risk. This skill organizes those steps for authorized security teams.
actual_capabilities: Outlines SSH service discovery with common and alternate ports.
Lists SSH configuration checks for algorithms, host keys, and authentication methods.
Documents credential testing workflows with Hydra, Medusa, Paramiko, and Metasploit.
Explains SSH local, remote, dynamic, and jump-host forwarding patterns.
Covers post-exploitation checks for SSH keys, sudo access, user lists, and shell history.
Provides quick reference tables for enumeration, brute-force, and forwarding commands.
limitations: The skill contains offensive workflows that require written authorization.
It does not enforce scope, rate limits, or safety checks automatically.
Commands may trigger lockouts, alerts, or service disruption.
It is guidance only and does not validate legal permission.

use_cases.title: Authorized Internal SSH Audit
use_cases.description: A security engineer reviews SSH exposure, algorithms, and authentication settings across approved internal hosts.

use_cases.title: Red Team Exercise Planning
use_cases.description: A red team operator maps SSH testing steps, tool choices, and documentation needs before an approved engagement.

use_cases.title: Hardening Verification
use_cases.description: A system administrator compares expected SSH hardening controls against assessment findings from an authorized test.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an SSH Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an authorized host list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an SSH audit checklist for these authorized hosts: [hosts]. Include discovery, configuration review, credential policy checks, and reporting sections.

prompt_templates.title: Review SSH Configuration Findings
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of collected audit output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these ssh-audit and Nmap SSH findings: [findings]. Prioritize weak algorithms, risky authentication methods, and practical hardening steps.

prompt_templates.title: Scope Credential Testing Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe credential testing plan for an approved SSH assessment. Include rate limits, lockout controls, user notifications, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Document Post-Exploitation Risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reporting after an authorized exercise.
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize SSH post-exploitation risks from these notes: [notes]. Focus on key exposure, sudo access, pivoting paths, persistence risk, and remediation.

output_examples.input: Authorized SSH audit notes show OpenSSH 7.2, password login enabled, weak ciphers, and root login disabled.
output_examples.output: The report would rank password authentication and weak ciphers as priority issues. It would recommend stronger algorithms, reduced login exposure, and monitored remediation.

output_examples.input: A red team needs to document SSH tunneling observed during an approved exercise.
output_examples.output: The output would explain local, remote, and dynamic forwarding paths. It would list affected internal services and containment recommendations.

output_examples.input: Post-exploitation notes mention readable authorized_keys, shell history with SSH commands, and sudo access.
output_examples.output: The summary would identify credential exposure, privilege risk, and persistence risk. It would recommend key rotation, history review, and sudo policy tightening.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, and stop conditions before using any workflow.
Prefer read-only configuration review before credential testing or post-exploitation checks.
Document every command, target, timestamp, and result for auditability.
anti_patterns: Do not run brute-force tests against systems outside the approved scope.
Do not add keys, alter SSH files, or create tunnels without explicit approval.
Do not use collected keys, passwords, or host data beyond the engagement rules.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for general marketplace use?
faq.answer: It contains offensive SSH testing workflows. Use should be limited to authorized security work.

faq.question: Does the skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown guide, but agents may repeat or adapt the commands.

faq.question: What tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Nmap, ssh-audit, Hydra, Medusa, Paramiko, Metasploit, and SSH forwarding.

faq.question: Can it help with defensive hardening?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help review SSH settings and translate findings into hardening actions.

faq.question: What is the main risk?
faq.answer: The main risk is misuse for credential attacks, pivoting, sensitive file access, or persistence.

faq.question: What permission is required?
faq.answer: Users need written authorization for every host, account, credential test, and post-access action.
